head: 6f49ae3a717e5521051704c7055016a3ae0ccefd
summary: Added four plant rows, F20-F23, to eng/rules-harness/plants.json, one for each of SL-043's twinned fitness entries. F20 covers TheClassifierListsNoLinkTags, F21 and F22 cover the Core and App halves of NothingWaitsOnTheVolumeFigure, and F23 covers TheVolumeReadHoldsNoScanStore. F20, F21 and F23 list their settled twins in `also_settled`, and F23 also lists SL-044's 'Core does not publish a live ScanStore before the scan ends'. I updated the `_note` counts to 39 rows and 23 must-fire, and left the hand-only outcomes sentence word for word. I then made the recording run: harness.py with --engine-root set to the taad_v3 checkout at faecfc3 and --scenario all, against the edited tree. It exited 0 with 52 rows, 52 AS-RECORDED and 0 stray hits, and a clean baseline of 11 Facts with 0 hits, 64 rules and 0 hits. Its stdout and details are saved under .taad/slices/SL-075/. RuleCases.ps1 had no literal that counts plants.json rows. The only change there is a decoy-engine check in C-006, so that O-008's shape is actually fed in. The whole RuleCases suite and rules-parity both pass.

files.why: Adds rows F20-F23, with `also_settled` where the plant also breaks a settled rule, plus row notes saying which parts were transcribed from the spike and which were re-derived. The `_note` counts go from 35/19 to 39/23 (F01-F23), and the also_settled sentence now covers F20, F21 and F23.

C-006 gets two decoy-engine checks. First, with a second taad3 package on PYTHONPATH, `--scenario clean` still loads taad3.fitness from --engine-root: the header names <root>\taad3\fitness.py, and the run exits 0 CLEAN. Second, it bites: a decoy already imported through sitecustomize makes the harness exit 2 with 'taad3.fitness was imported from <decoy>, not from this root'. No count literal was changed, because none exists.

Record of the recording run: command, exit 0, summary line, clean-baseline line, engine root/module/HEAD faecfc3 (clean), interpreter, dotnet source, repo HEAD, and which parts are re-derived. Written after all harness runs had finished.
Full stdout of the recording run: 52 rows AS-RECORDED, exit 0.

obligations.how: Row F20 plants `private const uint IO_REPARSE_TAG_SYMLINK = 0xA000000C;` after the class's opening brace in EntryClassifier.cs, which puts it at line 23, the line where the spike's trx failed. `also_settled` names 'the classifier does not list link tags; the surrogate bit is the rule'. `harness.py --only F20` gives fire/fire, AS-RECORDED, 0 stray hits, exit 0. In the --scenario all run, F20 shares a batch with P07d, and P07d stays quiet/quiet AS-RECORDED.

Row F21 plants `_store.VolumeUsedSource.Task.Wait();` in Scanner.cs, after the VolumeSpace.Start line. Its rule is 'NothingWaitsOnTheVolumeFigure (Core)', and `also_settled` names 'nothing in Core waits on the volume figure'. `--only F21` gives AS-RECORDED with 0 stray hits, exit 0. judge() counts any unnamed rule that fires as a STRAY-HIT, so the App entry stayed silent.

Row F22 plants `result.Store.VolumeUsed.Wait();` in MainWindow.xaml.cs, after the ShowVolumeInUse line. Its rule is 'NothingWaitsOnTheVolumeFigure (App)'. `--only F22` gives xUnit fire (the one Fact) and Fitness fire, with only the App entry: AS-RECORDED, 0 stray hits, exit 0. So the Core entry and every settled rule stayed silent, including 'the window never touches the scan store', whose lookbehind allows `result.Store`.

`--only F21,F22` runs both plants in one batch. The harness gives each hit to the row whose planted lines it falls in, and judge() matches the exact rule strings 'NothingWaitsOnTheVolumeFigure (Core)' and '(App)'. Both rows came out AS-RECORDED with 0 stray hits, exit 0, so each string names its own entry and not the other.

Row F23 plants `Store.ScanStore? store = null;` in VolumeSpace.cs, after the `read = reader ?? Read` line. `also_settled` names 'the volume read cannot hold a scan's memory' and 'Core does not publish a live ScanStore before the scan ends'. `--only F23` gives AS-RECORDED, 0 stray hits, exit 0. judge() requires every name in `also_settled` to fire, so both settled rules fired.

`harness.py --scenario clean` on the edited tree gives: xunit 11 Facts, 0 hits | fitness unable, 64 rules, 117 files read, 0 hits, none unmatched, CLEAN, exit 0. The only rule not run is the import rule the design accepts.

`--scenario all` with the committed 39-row plants.json and divergences.json unchanged gives 52 rows, 52 AS-RECORDED, 0 not, 0 stray hits, exit 0. F01-F19, P07c-e, S01-S13 and D1-D13 all kept their recorded outcomes. I ran it twice, once with --dotnet-from SL-074 and once on this tree's own .dotnet, with the same result.

Every run's header reads 'taad3.fitness from C:\Users\sshub\projets\taad_v3\backend\taad3\fitness.py'. I added a decoy check to RuleCases C-006. With a second taad3 on PYTHONPATH, the header still names the engine root and the run is CLEAN, exit 0. With a decoy pre-imported through sitecustomize, the harness exits 2 with 'imported from <decoy>, not from this root', and the decoy's check() is never called. `RuleCases.ps1 -Case C-006` gives all checks held, exit 0. The ~/.claude venv was not used.

I searched RuleCases.ps1 for 35, 19, 48, 52, F17, F19, plants.json and must-fire. Nothing counts plants.json rows. C-008's $MustFire is SL-022's F01-F16, passed through --only, and C-009 names P07c-P07e. So no literal needed moving. `RuleCases.ps1 -Case All` with the engine gives C-001 to C-014 all checks held, exit 0, 300 s.

`pwsh -NoProfile -File eng/rules-parity.ps1` gives 'rules-parity: AGREE 11 facts <- 15 twinned entries, 27 patterns; 49 settled entries', exit 0. Only plants.json and RuleCases.ps1 changed (git diff --stat).

This obligation is aimed at validate-slice; I am reporting evidence for it. The committed plants.json, not a scratch file, was run under --scenario all: 52/52 AS-RECORDED, and the existing 48 rows did not move. See .taad/slices/SL-075/recording-run.stdout.txt.

This obligation is aimed at validate-slice; I am reporting evidence for it. A .NET 10 SDK was reachable both ways. --dotnet-from SL-074 (.dotnet/sdk/10.0.401) built the scratch copy in 8 s. eng/dotnet.ps1 also populated this tree's gitignored .dotnet/sdk/10.0.401 during RuleCases C-006 (Q-003), and every later run used that.

cases.test_name: tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1::Case-C006 (decoy taad3 on PYTHONPATH / preloaded via sitecustomize)

deviations: RuleCases.ps1: the design expected count literals to bump by +4. None exist. C-008's $MustFire is SL-022's F01-F16 (1..16), passed through --only, not a count of plants.json rows. C-009 names P07c-P07e. Neither moves with new rows, and the design did not know this (the survey had not listed the literals). The one edit is two decoy-engine checks in C-006. Without them no test fed O-008's shape (taad3.fitness importable from somewhere other than the engine root): C-006 already covered missing, non-engine, broken and short-result roots, but not a second importable taad3.

Re-derived rather than transcribed (design amendment 1). The spike record was clipped, and its kept plants-spike.json was not under %TEMP% (I searched fsa-rules-* and a depth-4 search for plants-spike*.json). F21's text is the spike's X02 text, but its anchor (the VolumeSpace.Start line in Scanner.cs) is re-derived. F22's text and file (MainWindow.xaml.cs, after the ShowVolumeInUse line) and F23's text (`Store.ScanStore? store = null;` in VolumeSpace.cs) are re-derived. Each row's note says so, and the recording run passed on them as committed. F20's text is the spike's own. Its anchor '{' puts it at line 23, the line the spike's trx named.

The `_note` change goes beyond the two counts. It also says F20-F23 are one row per SL-043 entry, and extends the also_settled sentence to cover F20, F21 and F23. This follows how SL-040 and SL-069 documented their rows. The sentence 'Outcomes come from the recorded runs and are changed by hand only.' is unchanged.

follow_ups: RuleCases.ps1 C-008 exercises only F01-F16 ($MustFire = 1..16). F17-F23, SL-040's and SL-075's must-fire rows, are measured only by a plain harness --scenario plants/all run, and no rule case shows them biting. Deriving $MustFire from the F-rows in plants.json would cover them.

Risk spikes that write scratch plants files should save them into the slice folder. spikes#62's plants-spike.json could not be found, so F21's anchor and all of F22 and F23 had to be re-derived instead of transcribed.

F20 anchors on the first line of EntryClassifier.cs that is only '{' (the class brace). If a bare '{' line is ever added above the class, the plant moves without warning. A more specific anchor would need a line in the file that is unique and safe to insert after.
